doc.title: Richard Wyands interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

title: Playing at the Blackhawk opposite big names
summary: With bassist Vernon Alley he played intermissions and sets opposite Peterson, Roach and Shearing, making contacts.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: I understand you played at the Blackhawk backing up different musicians that would come in?
That must have been a good experience.

It was because I got a chance, even if I wasn’t backing them up, if I didn’t back then up I was playing intermissions piano, or with a trio or duo. There was a bass player, well he’s still there, Vernon Alley. He and I worked at the Blackhawk, either with a quintet, quartet or duo, opposite these big name acts, like Oscar Peterson, Max Roach, George Shearing, a long list. It was a great experience because I got a chance to sit there every night and watch and listen to all of these great musicians. And sometimes they’d invite me up to play with them.
